title: Fuzzing Lab
prompt: Add fuzz tests to a string parser and fix discovered edge cases. Apply the material from “Subtests and Test Organization”. Work only in a local project you control; external services are not needed unless the prompt explicitly says so.

starter.code:
package parser

// TODO: define the parser contract, seed normal/invalid inputs, and implement a fuzz test.

files.name: parser.go
files.content:
package parser

// TODO: define the parser contract, seed normal/invalid inputs, and implement a fuzz test.

expected_output: No crash for seeded inputs; run duration depends on environment
hints: Restate the input, normal result, and one boundary case before coding.
Use Fuzz only where it clarifies the solution; keep each function focused and check returned errors.
Run gofmt, then write or run tests for both the usual input and a failure/edge case.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation addresses the stated objective: Add fuzz tests to a string parser and fix discovered edge cases.
Normal-case output or behavior matches documented acceptance criteria.
At least one boundary, invalid-input, or dependency-failure case is handled deliberately.
Code is formatted, errors are handled, and setup/test instructions are reproducible.

test_cases.name: normal case
test_cases.input: Use the representative sample input described in the project README or exercise prompt.
test_cases.expected: No crash for seeded inputs; run duration depends on environment

test_cases.name: boundary or failure case
test_cases.input: Try an empty input, malformed record, missing file, invalid range, or external-operation failure relevant to the task.
test_cases.expected: The program reports or handles the condition deliberately and does not claim success.

public_tests.name: normal case
public_tests.description: Check the requested behavior for a representative input.

public_tests.name: boundary case
public_tests.description: Check the expected safe behavior when input or an operation is invalid.

execution_mode: static-validation; arbitrary learner code requires a separate isolated runner with timeouts, resource limits, and explicit filesystem/network policy.

retry_policy.feedback: Read the first failed acceptance criterion, change one cause, and retest.

status_note: Human review required. Static token checks are preliminary and do not execute arbitrary Go source.
